Taking care of your health is a lifelong journey. Many times, we only go to a clinic when we fall sick or feel pain. However, waiting for symptoms to appear is not always the best way to stay healthy. Silent conditions like high blood pressure, fatty liver, or early diabetes do not show warning signs right away. This is why preventive checkups are so valuable. If you want to track your fitness levels safely, choosing Silver Touch Hospitals, the best hospital for full body checkup in Ahmedabad,helps you get clear answers about your health status.

The big question many people ask is whether they truly need to repeat these extensive health medical tests every twelve months. The answer is not identical for everyone. Your ideal health screening timeline changes based on your age, your regular lifestyle habits, and your family medical history.

Age Guidelines for Annual Screening

If you are a healthy person below the age of thirty with no health problems whatsoever, you may not need a full body scan on an annual basis. Just having yourself checked out once every two or three years should suffice for checking on your overall fitness levels.

However, once you cross the age of thirty, your body baseline begins to change. The medical team at Silver Touch Hospitals strongly advises adults over thirty to get a complete body checkup every year. This regular timeline becomes even more important for senior citizens who need to track their organ functions closely.

Here’s what to remember:

  • Under 30 Years Old ──► Checkup every 2 to 3 years
  • Over 30 Years Old ──► Checkup every single year
  • Chronic Conditions ──► Frequent tracking as advised

Understanding Personal Risk Profiles

The frequency at which you visit the clinic depends highly on your lifestyle. People with a sedentary lifestyle working from office desks, high-stress individuals, and people with a history of cardiac problems in their family must never miss their yearly assessments.

At Silver Touch Hospitals, we do all of this in one package. This includes assessment of blood glucose levels, total lipid profile, liver function tests, and cardiovascular assessment using electrocardiogram tests.
